title: What is your "game ready" asset workflow?
author: exogreek
selftext:
Hello! One of the more conservative AI users here, been in devops for many years so know my way around code and am pretty decent at negating the AI slop one could generate on the code side of my projects. The one thing I struggle with is asset creation. I am learning blender currently but I do see quite a bit of AI generated stuff that would seemingly make grey boxing maps for my current project better. I am wondering what you guys are using for workflows/pipelines that take prompts and/or reference images and turn them into multi-view generations that have some semblance of proper topology. IE if I want to create some simple world props like a map that my character can hold, or a telescope, etc, what would your current workflow or process be?

Not really wanting to just let opus or astra run wild as those are currently generating terrible topology and at that rate/cost id be far better off just making them myself. I am also not opposed to workflows that cost some money as I already have a publisher agreement for my current game so any spend would come from funds allocated to me for development.

Thanks dudes, drop any wisdom you can, looking to cut out as much of the simple stuff as I dive deeper into the mechanics that require my actual attention!

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: I make full assets before execution for the intended roadmap and blueprint I have created, along with the concept art of how I want the game constructed, it helps guide the agent when deciding things like placement, perspective, etc.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
I make full assets before execution for the intended roadmap and blueprint I have created, along with the concept art of how I want the game constructed, it helps guide the agent when deciding things like placement, perspective, etc

I have created a model that is trained on thousands of images of my art styling (I've been doing comics since the 80s as a hobbyist), and then I created a very detaild 'Universal Art Guide' for all of my projects. One for each style/vibe/concept. 

Then I provide the agent with the art guide, my roadmap, and my blueprint, and ask the agent to generate a prompt shopping list I will then feed to my art model and pump out the aforementioned assets before beginning.

replies.author: exogreek
replies.body: Ok so you run your own pipeline that iterates off of your specific style? Does this do the full 3D generation, or is this strictly 2D? I guess I should have specified im looking or 3D workflows if so :)

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body:
I am currently building 2D and 2.5D games (this all began for my kid and then became a thing lol) but I would imagine moving this to a 3D format would be simple enough. It's more about the workflow than the specific tools I guess. 

In either case I personally do not advocate permitting the model to simply decide what is best for the project on any level so your instinct here is solid. 

Good luck, I hope you find your groove.

comments.author: Murph4321
comments.body: What's worked for me really is using an image generator to make an image you want and tailor it till it looks how you want. Then put it to an image to 3d mesh generator like tripo. Then export your mesh from tripo to blender and get an ai like gpt or claude to fix topology and stuff like that. Works much better and quicker than getting ai to start from scratch in blender
